name: FortiGate OT Lab
tagline: A virtual Purdue-model factory with a FortiGate-VM as the only way in: segmentation, OT app control, OT IPS and virtual patching.
description: A fully virtual OT lab built along the **Purdue model**: a FortiGate-VM (FortiOS 7.6 with the OT licence) is the **only** connection between your physical network and five OT segments, from the OT-DMZ down to Level 0 field I/O, plus a test-center segment that plays the rogue IT host.

The installer creates a controller container with a web UI. The controller builds the bridges, deploys and licenses the FortiGate, clones the simulated PLCs, HMI, historian, OPC UA gateway and engineering workstation, and pushes the OT policy set. Afterwards it doubles as a **test center**: run the validation scenarios and see PASS/FAIL next to the matching FortiGate log lines.

The OT bridges have no physical port and the Proxmox host has no IP on them. The controller manages devices **out-of-band** via the hypervisor (`pct exec`), so the FortiGate really is the only network path in.

requirements.label: Hypervisor
requirements.value: Proxmox VE host with root shell access

requirements.label: Licence
requirements.value: FortiGate-VM `.lic` file or FortiFlex token — the lab uses 7 interfaces, so the eval licence is not enough — plus the OT Security Service

requirements.label: OT signature packages
requirements.value: `OTDB`, `OTDP`, `ISDB`, `IOTD` `.pkg` files from support.fortinet.com, uploaded once (pushed offline)

requirements.label: Controller
requirements.value: LXC · 2 vCPU · 2 GB RAM · 16 GB disk

requirements.label: Whole lab (approx.)
requirements.value: ≈ 10 GB RAM: FortiGate 2 vCPU / 4 GB, ~15 small LXCs (256–512 MB each)

requirements.label: Network
requirements.value: One bridge/VLAN for the controller and FortiGate port1; DHCP or a static IP

install.title: Interactive install
install.description: Choose **Default** or **Advanced**, just like the Proxmox community scripts. Advanced asks for name prefix, IDs, storage, bridge/VLAN, DHCP or static IP, UI port and VMID range, then shows a summary before anything is created. At the end it prints the web UI URL and password.

install.title: Unattended install
install.description: Same choices as environment variables — see the header of `install.sh` for the full list.
install.command:
OTLAB_UNATTENDED=1 CT_BRIDGE=vmbr1 CT_VLAN=40 CT_IP=10.40.0.240/24 CT_GW=10.40.0.1 CT_STORAGE=local-zfs \
  bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kay-arne/fortigate-ot-lab/main/install.sh)"

install.title: Update an existing controller
install.description: Re-running the one-liner detects the controller and offers **Update**; the running lab is not touched. Updating is also possible from the web UI (**Updates** tab).

steps: Open the web UI on the URL the installer printed and log in as `admin`.

**Setup**: upload the FortiGate `.qcow2`, choose the licence (`.lic` or FortiFlex token), set the port1 WAN IP and an admin password. Upload the OT signature packages under **Settings → OT signatures**.

**Lab → Deploy lab**: the controller creates the Purdue bridges (`vmbr900`–`vmbr999`), the FortiGate-VM via cloud-init, one LXC template with all OT simulators, the device clones and the full policy set.

Open the **Test center** to run the validation tests, and hand out the three access paths: FortiGate GUI, SSH as contractor via the jump host (MFA + session recording), and a viewer for HMI, historian and MES.
For a demo or training, follow the lab guide — a narrative walk-through (“a night at Polderfris”) with a lesson and IEC 62443 mapping per chapter.

features.title: Zones & conduits
features.description: Purdue levels as FortiGate ports; every conduit an explicit policy, everything else a logged implicit deny.

features.title: OT application control
features.description: Read-only Modbus from L3 and the OPC UA gateway — writes are blocked by the `OT-readonly` profile.

features.title: Virtual patching
features.description: A real Schneider UMAS DoS (CVE-2018-7846) against a simulated Modicon M580, dropped by the FortiGuard OT signatures — with a toggle to show the unpatched case.

features.title: Asset visibility
features.description: Devices carry vendor MAC OUIs and answer Modbus device identification, so Asset Identity Center and OT View fingerprint vendor and model.

features.title: Secure remote access
features.description: Contractor SSH through a DMZ jump host with MFA and session recording, then on to the engineering workstation.

features.title: “Break it” scenarios
features.description: IT-to-PLC attempts, recon scans, DMZ bypass, S7 stop, Shellshock on the MES and PLC-to-internet — each with expected result and log lines.

notes: The controller logs in to the host over **SSH** (`qm`, `pct`, `pvesh`). By default a dedicated `otlab` user with narrow sudo rules is created; revoke it any time with `otlab-revoke`. `qm`/`pct` are effectively root-equivalent, so treat this as visible and revocable, not as a sandbox.
The web UI is plain HTTP with a login form — keep it inside your lab network.
Linked clones need LVM-thin or ZFS; on `dir` storage the controller falls back to full clones.
Tear down with **Lab → Tear down…**; remove the controller itself with `pct destroy <id>` and then run `otlab-revoke`.
